newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

CANADA, Dec 13 - St.Lawrence river - It is reported that four vessels were delayed due to shortage of pilots overnight. The Laurentian pilotage authority reports heavy traffic as the basic cause of the shortage.
HONDURAS, Dec 16 - Puerto Cortes - One vessel loading bananas at berth. 15 Vessels due of which 10 to discharge/load containers, 5 to load bananas. No berthing delays expected.

MEXICO, Dec 17 - Tampico - Vessels in port, 1 dmt, 1 steel coils, 1 machinery, 1 general cargo, 1 zinc, 1 diesel, 1 lpg. 2 Vessels anchored of which 1 corn, 1 awaiting instructions. Port working normally. Altamira - Vessels in port, 1 general cargo, 1 container vessel. 3 Vessels anchored of which 1 container, 2 chemicals. Port working normally. Veracruz - Vessels in port, 4 grain, 1 steel, 3 containers, 2 pipes, 2 oil tankers, 1 repair, 3 sugar. Port working normally. Manzanillo - Vessels in port, 2 cars, 3 general cargo, 3 containers, 1 fertiliser. Port working normally. Coatzacoalcos - Vessels in port, 9 oil tankers, 5 chemicals.

PANAMA, Dec 16 - Panama Canal - The scheduled lock overhaul work is now in progress until 19 December. There was a breakdown 14/12 on one side of Gatun locks, and on 15/12 there was a breakdown on the only operating side of Miraflores locks. Transits are therefore already greatly affected and delays for vessels arriving on 16/12 are estimated at 2 days for vessels over 91 ft. beam and/or restricted, and for vessels under 91 ft. beam and not restricted, delays are 2.5-3 days. Relay lockages and crew augmentation is being provided to minimise delays. Balboa - One bulker in port. Cristobal - One container and 1 passenger vessel in port.
